newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on Yeltsin operation news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on Yeltsin operation news.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Tuesday on news President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery had been performed successfully as local traders marked prices up hoping for Western demand, but ended off early highs, brokers said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 1.89 percent to 183.95 on $22.97 million in volume.
Russian doctors performed a planned bypass heart surgery on Yeltsin on Tuesday and declared it a complete success. They said he would be able to resume normal work.
But market operators said the operation was only half the story.

"The success of the operation is only half of the deal. Very few doubted it would go wrong, but how the rehabiliation period will go on, that's the question," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
Doctors said it could take up to two months for Yeltsin to resume working.
Prices came off in afternoon trade after a morning rally initiated by Russian brokers who hoped for Western support on the operation news which never came.
Traders gave mixed opinions on the state of the market in the next few days.
Ippolitov said that it would take foreign investors about a week to see how Yeltsin recuperated and to decide whether to send more funds in Russia.
He forecast prices would be mixed on Wednesday and fall after the November 7-9 holidays.
Foreign investors thought that Russian shares were now overpriced and would wait for them to fall, creating another obstacle to a possible rise, Ippolitov said.
"New money is unlikely to come at this level," he said.
But Alexander Babayan, strategy investment director at CentreInvest Securities, said he saw a lot of Western demand in the second-tier shares.
"The market is in a very good, balanced condition," he said. "It is very healthy."
He forecast a price rise in the next few days.

St Petersburg Telephone was traded at $1.20 after $1.04 at Monday's close, Irkutskenergo rose to $0.108 from $0.104, LUKoil was $10.16 after $10.02, UES edged up to $0.0840 from $0.0830 and Rostelekom fell to $2.60 from $2.62.
